content: 1. The recommended loading dose of itraconazole should be determined based on pharmacokinetic data. Treatment should continue for a minimum of 3 months and until the active fungal infection has resolved. Insufficient treatment duration may result in recurrence of the infection. 2. Itraconazole is indicated for the treatment of blastomycosis, including both pulmonary and extrapulmonary infections, in immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised adults. 3. It is also indicated for the treatment of pulmonary and extrapulmonary aspergillosis in adults who are either intolerant to or have not responded to amphotericin B therapy. 4. Itraconazole is used to treat histoplasmosis, including chronic cavitary pulmonary disease and disseminated, non-meningeal histoplasmosis, in both immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised adults. 5. It is indicated for the treatment of onychomycosis of the toenail caused by Trichophyton rubrum or other dermatophytes. 6. In patients with conditions such as neutropenia, AIDS, or organ transplantation, oral bioavailability of itraconazole may be reduced. Dose adjustments should be made based on clinical response in these patients. 7. Itraconazole capsules and oral solution are not interchangeable. Only the oral solution has been proven effective for oral and/or esophageal candidiasis. 8. The safety and efficacy of itraconazole have not been established in certain populations or conditions. 9. Itraconazole increases the levels of alfuzosin by inhibiting its metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Itraconazole increases the levels of avanafil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Co-administration of itraconazole with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 12. Conivaptan increases itraconazole levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Itraconazole increases the levels of dihydroergotamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to an increased risk of ergotism, cerebral ischemia, and/or extremity ischemia. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Itraconazole increases the levels of disopyramide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Itraconazole increases the levels of dofetilide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Itraconazole increases the levels of dronedarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Itraconazole increases the levels of eliglustat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated in poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. 18. Itraconazole increases the levels of eplerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase the risk of hyperkalemia and hypotension. Co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Itraconazole increases the levels of ergotamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to an increased risk of ergotism, cerebral ischemia, and/or extremity ischemia. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Itraconazole increases the levels of estazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Felodipine increases itraconazole levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, and itraconazole increases felodipine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Itraconazole increases the levels of fesoterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment due to increased risk of severe adverse events. 23. Itraconazole increases the levels of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Itraconazole increases the levels of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to severe hypotension or syncope. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Itraconazole increases the levels of gepirone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Itraconazole increases the levels of irinotecan and its active metabolite SN-38 by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 27. Itraconazole increases the levels of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Itraconazole increases the levels of ivabradine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 29. Itraconazole increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 30. Itraconazole increases the levels of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Itraconazole increases the levels of lovastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 32. Itraconazole increases the levels of lurasidone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Itraconazole increases the levels of mavacamten by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 34. Itraconazole increases the levels of methadone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may result in QT interval prolongation and serious arrhythmias such as torsades de pointes. Co-administration is contraindicated. 35. Itraconazole increases the levels of methylergonovine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to an increased risk of ergotism, cerebral ischemia, and/or extremity ischemia. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Itraconazole increases the levels of midazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of oral midazolam is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. IV midazolam should be used with caution, and initial doses should be reduced. 37. Itraconazole increases the levels of naloxegol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may precipitate opioid withdrawal symptoms. Co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Itraconazole increases the levels of nisoldipine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Itraconazole increases the levels of pacritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Itraconazole increases the levels of pimozide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QT interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Itraconazole increases the levels of quinidine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QT interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 42. Itraconazole increases the levels of ranolazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase the risk of cardiovascular events, including QTc prolongation. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Itraconazole increases the levels of silodosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Itraconazole increases the levels of simvastatin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the risk of rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 45. Itraconazole increases the levels of solifenacin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment due to increased risk of severe adverse events. 46. Itraconazole increases the levels of ticagrelor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during and for 2 weeks after itraconazole treatment. 47. Itraconazole increases the levels of tolvaptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 48. Itraconazole increases the levels of triazolam by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to QT interval prolongation. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Itraconazole increases the levels of ubrogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Itraconazole increases the levels of venetoclax by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. 51. Itraconazole increases the levels of voclosporin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 52. Itraconazole increases the levels of acalabrutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 53. Itraconazole increases the levels of adagrasib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 54. Itraconazole increases the levels of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 55. Itraconazole increases the levels of afatinib by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. 56. Itraconazole increases the levels of aliskiren by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
